tiers.name: Run
tiers.what: code, data and weights released; execute or evaluate

tiers.name: Retrain
tiers.what: code and data released, no released weights; train before evaluating

tiers.name: Reimplement
tiers.what: no released code; rebuild the method from the paper

papers.claim: Collective Counterfactual Explanations (CCE) achieves better trade-off between individual modification cost and competition cost compared to standard counterfactual explanation methods, by incorporating a population dynamics model from mean-field game theory to penalize deviations from equilibrium.
papers.target: Combined cost (modification cost + λ₂×χ²-divergence) = CCE achieves best combined cost (lowest red bar in Figure 5) on Average across 100 experiments on Moons dataset, direction
papers.gist: Collective Counterfactual Explanations (CCE): counterfactuals are chosen via an entropic unbalanced-optimal-transport plan from the negative class to the positive class, trading individual modification cost against a competition/crowding cost (chi-squared divergence of the counterfactual distribution from the positive-class density), rather than each point independently seeking its nearest flip like standard CE methods.

papers.claim: EF-3DGS integrates event cameras with 3DGS for free-trajectory scene reconstruction, achieving up to 3dB higher PSNR and 40% lower ATE compared to state-of-the-art methods in high-speed/low-frame-rate scenarios.
papers.target: PSNR (novel view synthesis) and ATE (pose accuracy) vs state-of-the-art baselines at 1 FPS = up to 3dB higher PSNR and 40% lower ATE than SOTA under high-speed scenarios (abstract; Tables 1-2 at 1 FPS; NOTE arXiv v2 abstract states 2dB - repin must pin scene-level table numbers) on Single Tanks and Temples scene, 1 FPS event-frame hybrid protocol, direction
papers.gist: EF-3DGS (Event-Aided Free-Trajectory 3D Gaussian Splatting): integrates event-camera signals into a progressive 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline (built on CF-3DGS) via an event-generation-model loss, a contrast-maximization pose-refinement term, and photometric bundle adjustment, claiming better novel-view PSNR and camera-trajectory accuracy than SOTA at low frame rates on Tanks and Temples.

papers.claim: TabDPT achieves strong performance on both regression (CTR23) and classification (CC18) benchmarks, with scaling laws showing consistent performance improvements from both model and data size increases.
papers.target: CC18 AUC / CTR23 R2 = AUC >= 0.92 (paper 0.933) on CC18; R2 >= 0.70 (paper 0.742) on CTR23 on OpenML CC18 classification + CTR23 regression subsets, threshold
papers.gist: TabDPT: a tabular foundation model (76M/78M params, 16 layers, emsize 768, 600K pre-training steps) that does in-context learning over retrieved neighbours for tabular classification and regression, evaluated on the OpenML CC18 (72 datasets) and CTR23 (35 datasets) suites. Table 1: CC18 AUC 0.933 [0.929,0.937] and Accuracy 0.884 [0.882,0.887]; CTR23 Correlation 0.837 [0.826,0.848] and R2 0.742 [0.731,0.754].

papers.claim: RePO (Rectified Policy Optimization) algorithm outperforms baseline methods (SafeRLHF, SACPO) in LLM safety alignment by using critical safety constraints instead of expected safety constraints, achieving 96.08% safety rate vs 90.58% (SafeRLHF) on Alpaca-7B while also improving helpfulness (+1.01 vs -0.71).
papers.target: safety rate (fraction of responses with cost <= 0) on PKU-SafeRLHF test set = >90% safety rate, above the SafeRLHF baseline (paper Table 1: RePO 96.08% vs SafeRLHF 90.58% on Alpaca-7B) on PKU-SafeRLHF test set, Alpaca-7B RePO 1-epoch run, threshold
papers.gist: RePO: a safe-RLHF algorithm for LLM alignment that jointly optimizes helpfulness and safety via a reward model and a cost model alongside actor/critic policies, fine-tuning Alpaca-7B on PKU-SafeRLHF preference data.

papers.claim: SPARTAN learns accurate local causal graphs (low SHD) through sparsity regularisation while maintaining Transformer-level prediction accuracy, enabling improved few-shot adaptation and robustness.
papers.target: Structural Hamming Distance (SHD) of learned causal graph vs ground truth = 1.51 on Interventional Pong test set, direction
papers.gist: SPARTAN: a world model that learns sparse, interpretable per-object local causal graphs via a Gumbel-sigmoid hard-attention transformer with a sparsity-regularized Lagrangian objective, evaluated on a modified 'Interventional Pong' environment (dynamics interventions per Appendix Table 4) against a dense soft-attention Transformer baseline.

papers.claim: AlphaZero agents trained on board games produce game states that follow Zipf's law (frequency distribution S(n) ∝ 1/n^α with α ≈ 0.8-1.0), and agents optimize state loss in descending order of frequency.
papers.target: Zipf power-law exponent alpha = approx 0.8-1.0 (observed 0.75-1.05) on Connect Four state frequencies (Figure 1), range
papers.gist: AlphaZero Neural Scaling and Zipf's Law: self-play board-game states visited by AlphaZero agents follow a Zipf power law, state frequency S(n) proportional to n^-alpha with alpha around 0.8-1.0, and the paper links that power-law data distribution to the observed neural scaling laws. Connect Four and Pentago, Figure 1 shows the state-frequency rank curves.

papers.claim: The exact analytical solution for multi-reference RLHF (both RKL and FKL objectives) outperforms both single reference approaches and the MRPO approximation, achieving a 66.1% win rate when combining both references.
papers.target: Win rate against preferred answer (%) = 66.1% on UltraFeedback dataset (10% held-out for evaluation), direction
papers.gist: Proposes multi-reference RKL-regularized DPO: instead of aligning a policy against a single reference model, align it against a geometric-mean combination of two reference models (e.g. an SFT checkpoint and a larger instruct model), claiming this improves alignment quality over single-reference DPO.

papers.claim: LayerNorm Scaling (LNS), which scales the output of Layer Normalization by 1/sqrt(l) inversely proportional to layer depth, consistently outperforms Pre-LN and other normalization techniques in LLM pre-training, reducing perplexity across model sizes from 130M to 7B.
papers.target: Validation perplexity (lower is better) = 25.76 on C4 validation set, point estimate
papers.gist: The Curse of Depth in LLMs. Pre-LN makes output variance grow with depth, so deep blocks degenerate toward identity and contribute little. The fix, LayerNorm Scaling (LNS), multiplies each LayerNorm output by 1/sqrt(layer_index+1). Table 1 reports LLaMA-family pretraining perplexity on the provenance check for Pre-LN vs Pre-LN+LNS across 130M/250M/350M/1B.

papers.claim: EquiTabPFN, a target-permutation equivariant prior-fitted network, enables in-context learning on tabular datasets with arbitrary class counts, achieving 27.9% median relative accuracy (best among all methods) on datasets with more classes than seen during pre-training, while maintaining competitive performance on seen class counts with lower computational overhead than TabPFN with ECOC.
papers.target: Mean accuracy (%) on 10 TabZilla datasets with more than 10 classes = 77.0 +/- 1.8% on 10 TabZilla benchmark datasets with more than 10 classes (arrhythmaria taskId 5, 12 classes; soybean taskId 41, 19 classes; vowel taskId 3022, 11 classes; isolet taskId 3481, 26 classes; etc.), averaged over 10 random splits per dataset, point estimate
papers.gist: EquiTabPFN. Tabular foundation models such as TabPFN are limited to a fixed maximum number of target classes; the paper introduces an equivariant decoder over target dimensions so a single pretrained model handles arbitrary class counts without ensembling or padding tricks. The headline evidence is TabZilla out-of-distribution benchmarks split by class count.

papers.claim: A boosting-style algorithm that combines synthetic data with weak (beta>0) exogenously-labeled data converges to an optimal LLM, with focusing labeling resources on the most challenging examples leading to improved performance over filter-only approaches like STaR/ReST.
papers.target: test accuracy (greedy decoding) = 0.456 on GSM8K test set, point estimate
papers.gist: "Escaping Collapse: The Strength of Weak Data for Large Language Model Training" presents Algorithm 2, a boosting-style meta-algorithm for fine-tuning LLMs on self-generated data: a weak-labeler weighting scheme (theta=log(1/(1-beta))) concentrates training weight on problems the previous round's model still gets wrong, across rounds of fine-tuning. The paper argues this boosting procedure beats a Filter-only baseline (STaR/ReST-style: train only on the model's own already-correct samples) and a Do-nothing baseline, on GSM8K and MBPP with Gemma-2-2B.

papers.claim: A minimalist two-layer neural network with two-dimensional input (one relevant feature x2, one irrelevant feature x1) exhibits progressive sharpening and self-stabilization phenomena under large learning rates, with sharpness oscillating around 2/eta while loss decreases non-monotonically.
papers.target: Sharpness S(theta) oscillation pattern = Sharpness oscillates around 2/eta=40 with periodic spikes and self-stabilization cycles (theoretical bound: 1.5/eta <= S(theta) <= 4.71/eta) on Synthetic 2D Gaussian regression, point estimate
papers.gist: "A Minimalist Example of Edge-of-Stability and Progressive Sharpening" (Liu, Zhang, Du, Zhao; Georgia Tech / UW) is a purely theoretical paper: a 2-layer, width-one linear network with 2D Gaussian input (one relevant, one irrelevant feature) is used to rigorously prove Progressive Sharpening and self-stabilizing Edge-of-Stability (EoS) dynamics under large-learning-rate gradient descent, with a non-asymptotic analysis of sharpness along the whole GD trajectory. There is no released code or dataset; Figure 1 is a synthetic deterministic simulation defined entirely by the paper's own closed-form update equations.

papers.claim: Týr-the-Pruner achieves 97% performance retention with 50% parameter pruning on Llama-3.1-70B while maintaining comparable language comprehension and downstream task performance.
papers.target: Wikitext2 perplexity (lower is better) = 16.17 on Wikitext2 test set, threshold
papers.gist: Tyr-the-Pruner builds a layerwise-sparsity 'supernet' via local OBS-style pruning, then searches sparsity distributions across layers with an evolutionary algorithm (a distillation-inspired KL fitness) to find high-quality structured pruning configurations at a target global sparsity.

papers.claim: The Fuse-and-Refine module enhances existing feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting models by merging and refining primitives in a canonical 3D space, achieving ~2 dB PSNR improvement over GS-LRM while running at interactive rates on a single GPU.
papers.target: PSNR (dB) = 30.61 on DL3DV test set, threshold
papers.gist: SplatVoxel ('Learning Efficient Fuse-and-Refine for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting', NeurIPS 2025). Proposes a hybrid Splat-to-Voxel 'Fuse-and-Refine' module, implemented in JAX, that refines feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions built on top of GS-LRM.

papers.claim: CQ-DINO achieves superior performance on vast vocabulary object detection (V3Det, 13,204 categories) by mitigating gradient dilution via learnable category queries with image-guided query selection, surpassing previous methods by 2.1% AP while maintaining competitive results on COCO.
papers.target: Average Precision (AP) = 46.3% on V3Det validation set, point estimate
papers.gist: CQ-DINO: category-query DINO for vast-vocabulary object detection. It replaces one-vs-all classification with learnable category queries plus an image-guided query selection and a category tree, arguing this mitigates gradient dilution when the label space is huge. Table 1 on V3Det (13,204 categories, 29,821 val images) reports CQ-DINO Swin-B at 24 epochs reaching 46.3 AP / 51.5 AP50 / 48.4 AP75, versus DINO's 42.0 AP.

papers.claim: FreeInv (random latent transformation during DDIM inversion/reconstruction) effectively reduces trajectory deviation and improves reconstruction fidelity with negligible computational overhead compared to standard DDIM inversion.
papers.target: PSNR (dB) = 27.69 on PIE benchmark (700 images, 512x512), point estimate
papers.gist: FreeInv: a training-free improvement to DDIM inversion for diffusion image editing. A random latent transformation (rotation by an angle drawn from {0,90,180,270}) is applied at each inversion step and replayed identically during reconstruction, which approximates a trajectory ensemble at negligible cost and reduces inversion-reconstruction deviation. Evaluated on PIE-Bench (700 images, 10 edit categories) with Stable Diffusion 1.5 and 50-step DDIM.

papers.claim: Activated LoRA (aLoRA) achieves competitive accuracy with standard LoRA while significantly reducing inference costs through KV cache reuse, demonstrating speedups up to 35x for evaluator tasks in agentic pipelines.
papers.target: Classification accuracy (%) = 79.30% (LoRA) vs 81.94% (aLoRA) on Test split of Bengali Hate Speech Classification dataset, direction
papers.gist: Activated LoRA (aLoRA): a LoRA variant whose adapter weights only activate after an 'invocation sequence' in the input, so the base model's KV cache up to that point can be reused. Table 6 (line ~378 of main_neurips.tex) claims aLoRA matches or beats standard LoRA on several small classification tasks fine-tuned on Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B, e.g. Bengali Hate Speech Classification: LoRA=79.30% vs aLoRA=81.94% test accuracy.

papers.claim: Default MoE outperforms standard TopK routing by providing dense gradient updates to the router through EMA default vectors for non-activated experts, achieving faster convergence (9% fewer tokens to target perplexity of ~12) and higher benchmark scores without computational overhead.
papers.target: validation perplexity = 23.48 on FineWeb validation set, direction
papers.gist: Proposes 'Default MoE', an MoE routing scheme that feeds non-activated experts a learned EMA 'default vector' instead of zero, giving the router a denser gradient signal than standard TopK or Loss-Free Balancing routing and yielding faster convergence / lower validation perplexity at matched token counts.

papers.claim: Antidistillation sampling modifies a language model's next-token probability distribution to generate reasoning traces that resist model distillation while preserving the original model's utility.
papers.target: distilled student accuracy on GSM8K Platinum test set = ~40% on GSM8K Platinum test set, point estimate
papers.gist: Antidistillation sampling perturbs a reasoning teacher model's next-token distribution, guided by a proxy student's loss gradient, so that generated reasoning traces retain the teacher's task accuracy while making distilled students trained on those traces perform noticeably worse than on ordinary-sampled traces.

papers.claim: 1-shot RLVR with a single training example (π₁) on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B improves MATH500 accuracy from 36.0% to 73.6%, matching RLVR with 1209 examples (73.6%).
papers.target: MATH500 accuracy (%) = 73.6% on MATH500 test set (500 problems), point estimate
papers.gist: One-Shot RLVR: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B using a SINGLE training example (pi_1) lifts MATH500 accuracy from 36.0% to ~73.6%, matching RLVR trained on the 1.2k-example DeepScaleR subset. The trained pi_1 checkpoint is released on HF; the paper's own Qwen2.5-Eval the run controller (math_eval.py generation + evaluate.py grading with latex2sympy) is shipped in the repo along with the 500-problem MATH500 test.jsonl.

papers.claim: GVM (Gradient Variance Minimization) achieves 2-4x convergence speedup and improved final accuracy over vanilla RAFT++ for chain-of-thought reasoning fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning tasks.
papers.target: Average @ 8 accuracy on Math500 benchmark = ~71-73% (vs RAFT++ baseline ~66-69%) on Math500 benchmark test set, direction
papers.gist: Proposes GVM (Gradient Variance Minimization / DIBS), an adaptive sample-allocation scheme for RAFT-style rejection-sampling fine-tuning of LLM chain-of-thought reasoning: an E-step estimates per-prompt accept rate and gradient norm, then allocates more rollout samples to high-value prompts across subsequent M-steps, claimed to give 2-4x faster convergence and higher final accuracy than vanilla RAFT++ on math benchmarks.

papers.claim: Combining noising-based (Ns) and denoising-based (Dn) interventions in circuit discovery produces circuits with both faithfulness and completeness, whereas existing methods using Ns alone achieve faithfulness but lack completeness due to incomplete OR gate recovery.
papers.target: circuit completeness = performance degradation D(G\C || G) when the discovered circuit is ablated from the full graph = Ns+Dn yields higher completeness (larger degradation on removal) than Ns alone (direction); paper Tables 2-3, Fig 4 on IOI task on GPT2-small; provisional — relative comparison, repin must set task/margin/tolerance, direction
papers.gist: Mechanistic-interpretability paper on circuit discovery for GPT2-small IOI: shows that combining noising-based (Ns) and denoising-based (Dn) interventions in edge-attribution circuit discovery (Ns+Dn) yields circuits that are both faithful and more *complete* (larger output-KL degradation when the circuit is ablated from the full model) than Ns-only circuits, across three discovery methods (ACDC, EAP, EdgePruning) and six sparsity levels (100-5000 edges).

papers.claim: Parallel scaling with P parallel streams achieves similar performance effects as scaling model parameters by O(log P), while showing superior inference efficiency (up to 22× less memory increase and 6× less latency increase compared to parameter scaling).
papers.target: GSM8K accuracy (exact-match, lm-evaluation-harness gsm8k task) = ParScale-1.8B-P8 approx 38.4% vs P1 baseline approx 28.7% (paper Table 4); anchor = P8 GSM8K accuracy, with the P8>P1 log-P scaling gap as the falsifiable relation on Load released non-gated HF checkpoints with the repo custom modeling class, run standard lm-eval-harness GSM8K; report P1 and P8
papers.gist: ParScale (Parallel Scaling Law for Language Models): a new scaling axis that runs P diverse, learnable transformations of the input through the same model in parallel and aggregates the P outputs, arguing this is roughly equivalent to O(log P) parameter scaling with far less memory/latency cost. Releases pretrained checkpoints (Qwen2.5-architecture, 1.8B params, P in {1,2,4,8}) and a small custom-modeling GitHub repo (QwenLM/ParScale).

papers.claim: GiGPO achieves fine-grained credit assignment for LLM agents while preserving critic-free, low-memory, stable convergence properties, achieving >12% performance gains on ALFWorld and >9% on WebShop over GRPO.
papers.target: Success rate (%) = 86.7% on ALFWorld benchmark (averaged over 3 random seeds), point estimate
papers.gist: GiGPO (Group-in-Group Policy Optimization): critic-free RL for LLM agents that adds a step-level group advantage on top of GRPO's episode-level group, giving fine-grained per-action credit assignment over long horizons. Table 1 reports ALFWorld success 86.7% for GiGPO w/std on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct vs GRPO 72.8%, and 90.8% vs 77.6% for the 7B variants, with headline gains of >12% on ALFWorld and >9% on WebShop over GRPO.

papers.claim: msf-CNN achieves inference using approximately 50% less peak RAM compared to prior art MCUNetV2 and StreamNet on microcontrollers by finding optimal CNN layer fusion settings via graph-based shortest path optimization.
papers.target: Peak RAM usage = 8.56 kB on MBV2-w0.35 model (MobileNetV2 width=0.35, 144x144 input, 53 layers), point estimate
papers.gist: msf-CNN: patch-based multi-stage fusion for TinyML CNN inference on microcontrollers. A graph shortest-path/minimax search over layer-fusion configurations minimizes peak RAM; the compiled models are deployed via RIOT-ML + microTVM AOT to MCU boards. Table 3 (tbl:min_peak_mem) reports minimal peak RAM in kB for MBV2-w0.35 (8.56), MN2-vww5 (15.368), MN2-320K (51.164) against Vanilla/MCUNetV2/StreamNet baselines, backing the abstract's 50% (text: 65-87%) peak-RAM reduction claim.

papers.claim: CURE achieves efficient (~2 seconds) and effective concept unlearning in diffusion models using closed-form spectral orthogonal projection (Spectral Eraser), with minimal collateral damage to unrelated concepts.
papers.target: LPIPS_e (erasure LPIPS): perceptual distance between erased-model and original-model generations on target-concept prompts; higher = stronger concept removal = 0.41 (Table 1, Kelly McKernan artist-style removal row) on Single-concept (Kelly McKernan) style-erasure evaluation subset, data/prompts_erased_kelly.csv, as reported in Table 1, threshold
papers.gist: CURE: a fast (~2s), closed-form spectral concept-unlearning method for text-to-image diffusion models (SD v1.4) that erases artist styles or other concepts by editing only cross-attention key/value weights, evaluated via LPIPS_e (style-erasure strength) and LPIPS_u (utility preservation) plus COCO-30k FID/CLIP.

papers.claim: Toto achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot time series forecasting performance, with 13.1% lower MASE and 12.4% lower CRPS than the next best method on the BOOM observability benchmark.
papers.target: Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE) = 0.617 on BOOMlet benchmark, 32 metric queries, point estimate
papers.gist: Toto (Datadog): a 151M-parameter decoder-only foundation model for observability time series, released with BOOM, a benchmark of 2,807 real observability metric queries (7,416 eval instances) plus BOOMlet, a 32-query / 96-instance uniformly sampled subset. Headline: Toto is zero-shot SOTA on BOOM, MASE 0.617 / CRPS 0.375, beating Moirai_Base 0.710 / 0.428.

papers.claim: Mixture of Inputs (MoI) consistently improves text generation quality across multiple LLMs and benchmarks by preserving distributional information during autoregressive generation.
papers.target: Accuracy (%) = 59.53% on yzhuang/tinyzero-Countdown-Tasks-4 full dataset, direction
papers.gist: Mixture of Inputs (MoI): a training-free decoding modification that, after sampling a token, feeds the decoder a Bayesian-weighted blend of the sampled token embedding and the full next-token distribution rather than the discrete token alone, with the blend weight set by the normalized entropy of the distribution. Implemented as a patch to vLLM 0.8.5's V1 GPU model runner; evaluated on math/code/reasoning benchmarks including CountDown-4.

papers.claim: PKPO provides novel low-variance unbiased gradient estimators for optimizing pass@k performance, which solves more tasks than standard pass@1 optimization especially on hard problems where conventional approaches stall.
papers.target: empirical variance of gradient estimator = ~10x lower variance than alternatives on Toy Gaussian policy experiment with reward function g(x)=x² for 0≤x≤1 else 0, magnitude
papers.gist: PKPO (Pass@K Policy Optimization) derives novel low-variance unbiased gradient estimators for the pass@k RL training objective and evaluates them both in real LLM RL fine-tuning (math/code/reasoning) and in a toy Gaussian-policy variance study.

papers.claim: STaPLe enables smaller language models (7-8B parameters) to self-improve by discovering and learning latent principles for self-correction, achieving +8-10% in AlpacaEval win-rate, +0.3 on MT-Bench, and +19-23% principle-following win-rate on IFEval.
papers.target: IFEval principle-following win-rate = 65.6% on IFEval benchmark (541 prompts) with Prometheus-8x7B-v2.0 judge comparing refined response to initial policy response, threshold
papers.gist: STaPLe (Self-Taught Principle Learning): a bootstrapped self-improvement algorithm where an E-step mines candidate 'principles' from a small LM's own generations against preference data and keeps refined responses that improve over the base response (best-of-N hard-EM), and an M-step SFTs the model on {prompt, principle, refined response} trajectories so it learns to intrinsically self-correct at inference time, without an external critic.

papers.claim: GoRank gossip algorithm converges to true ranks at O(1/t) rate on arbitrary communication graph topologies, and GoTrim estimates trimmed means robustly despite outliers in the data.
papers.target: Average normalized absolute error |Rk(t) - rk| / n across all nodes = ~0.05 on GoRank estimate at iteration t=80000, averaged over 100 trials on 2D Grid graph, point estimate
papers.gist: The paper introduces GoRank and GoTrim, decentralized gossip algorithms for estimating ranks and trimmed means across a network without a central coordinator, with theoretical O(1/t) convergence guarantees claimed to hold on arbitrary graph topologies.

papers.claim: ADLM with anchored tokens (anchor network + denoising network) achieves significantly lower test perplexity than prior diffusion language models, narrowing the gap with autoregressive baselines and becoming the first DLM to exceed AR models in MAUVE score.
papers.target: test perplexity (PPL, lower is better) = 21.66 on OpenWebText test split, point estimate
papers.gist: Anchored Diffusion Language Model (ADLM). A two-stage architecture where an anchor network predicts anchor-token distributions and a denoiser conditions on them, trained with an anchored ELBO. The claim is that this closes much of the perplexity gap between diffusion LMs and autoregressive baselines on LM1B and OpenWebText.

papers.claim: VORTA achieves an end-to-end speedup of 1.76x without loss of quality on video diffusion transformers for text-to-video generation.
papers.target: end-to-end video generation latency speedup = 1.76x on VBench text-to-video evaluation, HunyuanVideo 5s 720p video, point estimate
papers.gist: VORTA: sparse attention for video diffusion transformers. A learned router blends three attention branches (full SDPA, coreset/low-resolution pooled, and sliding-window FlexAttention) per head and timestep, trained as a lightweight router on top of a frozen HunyuanVideo backbone. Table 1 reports HunyuanVideo 5s 720p sampling latency 1043.85s baseline vs 594.23s VORTA (1.7566x) with VBench 82.26 -> 82.59, i.e. speedup without quality loss.

papers.claim: Training overparameterized models with Langevin dynamics at inverse temperature β yields a generalization gap bounded by √((βE[L(θ₀)] + ln(1/δ))/N), independent of training time, dimensionality, or mixing.
papers.target: Generalization bound value (Equation 5 in paper, expectation form) = 0.60302 on MNIST binary classification, 99% confidence (δ=0.01), threshold
papers.gist: A generalization-bound paper for models trained with (continuous/discretized) Langevin dynamics at inverse temperature beta: the bound depends only on the expected loss at initialization, not on training time, dimensionality, or mixing -- a bound-in-expectation result (Eq. 5) validated empirically on MNIST/FMNIST with an SGLD training cross-check.

papers.claim: FHGS (Feature-Homogenized Gaussian Splatting) achieves superior multi-view feature fusion, noise suppression, and geometric reconstruction quality compared to existing 3DGS-based feature fusion methods while maintaining real-time rendering efficiency.
papers.target: PSNR (dB) on rendered novel views = 30.9 on DTU scan24 test views, point estimate
papers.gist: FHGS (Feature-Homogenized Gaussian Splatting), NeurIPS 2025 submission. Adds a feature-homogenization loss over SAM-derived per-pixel semantic features to 2DGS surfel splatting, with a custom CUDA rasterizer (non_diff_mechanism) carrying a non-differentiable feature path. Claims both better novel-view PSNR and much tighter cross-view feature consistency (FE) than 2DGS on DTU and other indoor scenes.

papers.claim: CAD-Coder generates valid, diverse, and complex CAD models from natural language descriptions using CadQuery code generation with chain-of-thought reasoning and geometric reward optimization, achieving Mean CD of 6.54 and Median CD of 0.17.
papers.target: Mean Chamfer Distance (×10³) = 6.54 on Text2CAD official test set, point estimate
papers.gist: CAD-Coder: a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model fine-tuned (SFT + chain-of-thought, then GRPO with a geometric reward) to emit executable CadQuery Python that builds a CAD solid from a natural-language description. Evaluated on the official Text2CAD test split by executing the generated code, sampling point clouds, and computing chamfer distance against the ground-truth CAD geometry.

papers.claim: Neural Block Linearization (NBL) replaces self-attention layers with linear approximations derived from Linear Minimum Mean Squared Error (LMMSE) estimators, achieving significant computational speed-ups while preserving competitive accuracy on reasoning benchmarks without fine-tuning.
papers.target: throughput speedup = 1.20x on Mistral-7B autoregressive token generation (2048 context + 2048 decode, batch size 1, A100 GPU), relative to baseline, point estimate
papers.gist: Proposes Neural Block Linearization (NBL): replace selected transformer self-attention layers with closed-form LMMSE linear estimators computed via CCA on calibration data, aiming to speed up autoregressive inference without any fine-tuning while preserving reasoning-benchmark accuracy.

papers.claim: SAM-R1, using SAM as a reward provider in a modified GRPO RL framework, enables multimodal models to perform fine-grained reasoning segmentation with only 3K training samples, achieving 60.2% gIoU on ReasonSeg zero-shot.
papers.target: gIoU on ReasonSeg zero-shot test = 60.2% on ReasonSeg zero-shot test set, point estimate
papers.gist: SAM-R1 proposes using SAM as an external segmentation-accuracy reward provider inside a modified GRPO RL loop, claiming that fine-tuning a multimodal model (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) with only 3K training samples yields 60.2% gIoU on zero-shot ReasonSeg test.

papers.claim: Permissioned LLMs (PermLLM) enforce access control in LLMs via domain-specific LoRA adapters, achieving high DDI (Domain Distinguishability Index) scores near 1.0 indicating that an external auditor can almost perfectly identify the active security domain.
papers.target: DDI AUC-ROC = 0.99 on WMDP (bio, chem, cyber domains), mean±std across domains, threshold
papers.gist: PermLLM: permissioned LLMs that enforce access control via domain-specific LoRA adapters, evaluated with a Domain Distinguishability Index (DDI) -- an AUC-ROC computed from membership-inference attacks that measures whether an external auditor can tell which security domain's adapter is currently active.

papers.claim: MGE-LDM is the first latent diffusion model to jointly address music generation, source imputation, and text-conditioned source extraction without relying on predefined instrument labels, achieving the lowest FAD (0.47) on Slakh2100 total generation among compared multi-track diffusion baselines.
papers.target: FAD (Fréchet Audio Distance) using VGGish embeddings = 0.47 on Slakh2100 S_A test set (225 tracks, bass+drums+guitar+piano stems only), point estimate
papers.gist: MGE-LDM. A latent diffusion model over a joint mixture/submixture/source representation that handles total generation, source imputation and text-conditioned source extraction in one model, trained across heterogeneous stem datasets. Table 1 reports Frechet Audio Distance for unconditional total generation on Slakh2100 subsets, with variants T_a through T_d differing in training corpus.

papers.claim: Spatial-MLLM significantly enhances visual-based 3D spatial intelligence of video MLLMs, achieving state-of-the-art performance on VSI-Bench (48.4% micro average in paper, 51.13% in v1.1 release) without requiring 3D or 2.5D inputs, by using a dual-encoder architecture combining semantic features from Qwen2.5-VL and structural features from VGGT.
papers.target: VSI-Bench micro average accuracy (All) = 51.13% on VSI-Bench test set (~5000 QA pairs from ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes), point estimate
papers.gist: Spatial-MLLM: adds a VGGT-based spatial (3D-structure) encoder alongside the standard 2D visual encoder of a Qwen2.5-VL backbone so that a multimodal LLM can do visual-based spatial reasoning from ordinary video, with no depth, point cloud or other 3D input at inference. Evaluated on VSI-Bench (5130 QA pairs over ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes) with 16 uniformly sampled frames.

papers.claim: BASE and G-BASE (practical Bayes-optimal membership inference attacks) achieve state-of-the-art membership inference attack performance comparable to or exceeding LiRA and RMIA while requiring significantly lower computational cost.
papers.target: membership-inference AUC on Cora GCN = ~82.45% AUC (paper Table 1; matching/exceeding RMIA at lower cost) on Cora dataset, 2-layer GCN target, online BASE attack, point estimate
papers.gist: The paper introduces BASE, a practical Bayes-optimal membership-inference attack for GNNs, shown theoretically equivalent to RMIA at gamma=1 but computationally cheaper.

papers.claim: The Unified Budget-Aware (UBA) learning rate schedule consistently outperforms commonly-used schedules (step, cosine, cyclical, OneCycle, BT, REX) across diverse vision and language tasks, spanning network architectures (ResNet, OLMo) and scales, under different training-iteration budgets.
papers.target: validation accuracy (%) = 94.57±0.33 on CIFAR10 test set, point estimate
papers.gist: 'Stepsize anything: A unified learning rate schedule for budgeted-iteration training' - proposes the UBA (Unified Budget-Aware) learning-rate schedule, a single-hyperparameter (phi) fitted-function schedule derived to be optimal for any fixed training budget.

papers.claim: LinearPatch (Hadamard transformation + channel-wise scaling fused into a symmetric matrix) revives layer-pruned LLMs by addressing activation magnitude mismatch, achieving up to 94.15% retained performance on LLaMA-3-8B with 5/32 layers pruned.
papers.target: Average perplexity on WikiText-2, C4, PTB = 24.59 on WikiText-2/C4/PTB PPL benchmarks, point estimate
papers.gist: LinearPatch fuses a Hadamard-space channel-wise scaling correction into a single symmetric matrix inserted at the boundary of pruned transformer layers, restoring lost quality in layer-pruned LLMs without any fine-tuning.

papers.claim: Prolonged reinforcement learning (ProRL) training expands a language model's reasoning boundary, discovering genuinely new solution pathways absent in the base model, especially on tasks where the base model initially struggles.
papers.target: Average pass@1 improvement on math benchmarks = 15.7% on AIME24, AIME25, AMC, MATH, Minerva, Olympiad Bench, direction
papers.gist: ProRL (Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B): prolonged RL training (verl + DAPO-style GRPO) of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on 136K verifiable problems across math/code/STEM/logic/instruction-following. Headline: +15.7% avg pass@1 on 6 math benchmarks (AIME24, AIME25, AMC, MATH, Minerva, OlympiadBench) over the base model (60.14% vs 44.45%). Both the trained checkpoint (nvidia/Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B) and the base model (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) are released on HuggingFace, so this is an eval-only reproduction target -- no retraining needed.

papers.claim: MiniMax-Remover achieves state-of-the-art video object removal with only 6 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance (CFG), significantly improving inference efficiency while maintaining high visual quality.
papers.target: SSIM (structural similarity) = 0.9842 on DAVIS validation set (90 videos), point estimate
papers.gist: MiniMax-Remover. A two-stage video object remover: a simplified DiT trained with a minimax objective so that few-step, CFG-free sampling still removes objects cleanly. The selling point is 6 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance while retaining background fidelity, quantified in Table 1 by a background-preservation SSIM and PSNR against the input video on DAVIS.

papers.claim: Robot-R1 uses reinforcement learning (GRPO) to train LVLMs for embodied reasoning in robotics, where models trained with Robot-R1 outperform SFT methods and a 7B Robot-R1 model surpasses GPT-4o on reasoning tasks related to low-level action control (movement and spatial reasoning).
papers.target: Spatial reasoning score (GPT-4o-judged, 0-3 scale) = 1.51 on Robot-R1 Bench - spatial reasoning task (in-distribution + out-of-distribution average), point estimate
papers.gist: Robot-R1: GRPO-trained Qwen2.5-VL-7B vision-language models for embodied/robot low-level action-control reasoning; the paper claims the RL-trained 7B model outperforms SFT baselines and even GPT-4o on spatial and movement reasoning (Robot-R1 Bench), and separately reports SpatialRGPT-Bench numbers for released base/SFT checkpoints (Table 6).

papers.claim: APA (Adversary Preferences Alignment) achieves significantly better black-box transferability (up to 77.48% avg ASR across 10 models) while maintaining high visual consistency compared to existing unrestricted adversarial attack methods like ACA.
papers.target: Black-box attack success rate (ASR) = >50% black-box ASR (paper 77.48% avg across 10 models) on transfer to MobileNetV2 / Inception-v3 targets, threshold
papers.gist: CVPR-style paper proposing APA (Adversary Preferences Alignment), a two-stage LoRA + diffusion framework for unrestricted adversarial-example generation: Stage 1 fine-tunes a per-image LoRA against a rule-based visual-similarity reward (visual_alignment.py); Stage 2 updates the image latent/prompt embedding against a white-box substitute classifier using trajectory- and step-wise rewards plus a diffusion-augmentation trick, to improve black-box transferability (attack_alignment.py).

papers.claim: Test-Time Projection Learning (TTPL) enables a neural combinatorial optimization model trained on small-scale (100-node) TSP instances to generalize to large-scale instances (up to 100K nodes) by learning a projection strategy that aligns test distributions with training distributions, without requiring model retraining.
papers.target: optimality gap (%) = 3.25% on TSP5K synthetic test set (16 instances), point estimate
papers.gist: TTPL (NeurIPS 2025, CIAM-Group): neural combinatorial optimization for VRPs trained on small instances (TSP100) fails to generalize to large ones; the paper uses an LLM-driven evolutionary search (EoH + GPT-4o-mini, 105 generations) to design a coordinate PROJECTION applied at test time to KNN subgraphs, letting a frozen TSP100-trained LEHD backbone solve TSP5K-TSP100K. The evolved projections are shipped hardcoded in projection.py, so the expensive LLM-evolution phase does not need re-running to test the reported test-time numbers.

papers.claim: GaRA-SAM, which uses gated-rank adaptation to dynamically adjust the effective rank of LoRA adapters based on input corruption, significantly outperforms prior work on robust segmentation benchmarks, surpassing the previous best IoU score by up to 21.3%p on ACDC real corrupted image dataset.
papers.code_url: https://github.com/cvlab-postech/RobustSAM (Robust-Seg training data construction, original RobustSAM repository for reference data splits)
papers.target: Intersection over Union (IoU) under degraded conditions = 77.0% on LVIS dataset with synthetic corruptions, point prompts, ViT-B backbone, point estimate
papers.gist: GaRA-SAM proposes gated-rank adapters (GaRA) for SAM: frozen ViT-B image encoder with dual Gumbel-Sigmoid gates on q/k/v of all 12 blocks that select between a low-rank (r=16) and high-rank (r=256) adapter component per input, so capacity adapts to corruption severity in degraded-image segmentation.

papers.claim: The conditioned CA mechanism (CA_Z) achieves the most robust AUC for detecting low-effort crowdsourcing workers across mixed crowds and multiple datasets, consistently outperforming baselines as the fraction of LLM-reliant agents increases.
papers.target: Area Under ROC Curve (AUC) = 0.91 on Toxicity labeling dataset with GPT-4-generated LLM samples, averaged over all tested (alpha_llm, alpha_r, alpha_b) combinations in Table 1, point estimate
papers.gist: Introduces a conditioned correlated-agreement score (CA_Z) to detect low-effort crowdsourcing workers who report LLM-generated labels instead of doing the labeling task themselves, evaluated by AUC against baseline detectors (OA, CA, OA_Z, Dawid-Skene EM) under simulated noisy crowds on real labeling datasets.

papers.claim: Random-Sampling-Learn, a simple baseline that randomly samples a core-set and fits a Ridge regression model, achieves 37.2% reduction in estimation gap compared to Random-Sampling under interpolation, and AIPW is the only method that consistently outperforms Random-Sampling in both interpolation and extrapolation settings.
papers.target: estimation gap reduction vs Random-Sampling (%) = 37.2% on Average across all 19 benchmarks, point estimate
papers.gist: Studies benchmark compression / prediction methods that estimate LLM benchmark accuracy from a small coreset of examples, and shows a simple Random-Sampling-Learn baseline (random coreset + Ridge) reduces estimation gap substantially versus plain Random-Sampling, with AIPW the only method robust to both interpolation and extrapolation model splits.

papers.claim: POCCO (Preference-Driven Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization with Conditional Computation) significantly outperforms prior neural MOCOP solvers (WE-CA, CNH) and classical MOEAs on multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems, achieving state-of-the-art normalized hypervolume (HV) across Bi-TSP, MOCVRP, MOKP, and Tri-TSP benchmarks.
papers.target: Normalized Hypervolume (HV) = 0.6411 on Bi-TSP50 test set (200 instances, normalized with reference [35,35]), direction
papers.gist: POCCO is a multi-objective combinatorial optimization neural solver built on a WE-CA/POMO backbone with an added mixture-of-experts conditional computation (CCO) block, trained with a pairwise preference-optimization loss so one model covers many preference weightings.

papers.claim: PhysioWave achieves state-of-the-art performance on physiological signal tasks using a wavelet-based architecture with adaptive multi-scale decomposition and frequency-guided masking for self-supervised learning.
papers.target: Classification accuracy (%) = 93.12% on EPN-612 test set, point estimate
papers.gist: PhysioWave: a wavelet-decomposition transformer foundation model for physiological signals, self-supervised pretrained on 823 GB of EMG and 182 GB of ECG with frequency-guided masking (FgM). Ablation Table 5 reports the 'with all' (pretrained backbone + FgM) PhysioWave-EMG Small (4.99M params) fine-tuned on EMG-EPN612 6-gesture classification; Table 3 'Ours-Small' carries the same cell.

papers.claim: SEAL (Self-Adapting Language Models) enables LLMs to self-adapt by generating their own synthetic training data and update directives (self-edits) through reinforcement learning, improving knowledge incorporation accuracy from 33.5% to 47.0% on no-context SQuAD QA.
papers.target: no-context SQuAD QA accuracy (knowledge incorporation) = paper full-scale: base 33.5% -> SEAL 47.0%; anchor = SEAL-trained model beats the frozen base model's no-context accuracy on the same 50-passage eval by a clear positive margin (reduced-scale run; exact 13.5pt delta not expected) on reduced-scale single-passage SEAL knowledge incorporation, 50 SQuAD passages, 2 RL rounds, direction
papers.gist: SEAL (Self-Adapting Language Models): an LLM generates its own 'self-edits' (synthetic finetuning data/directives) and is trained via reinforcement learning (ReST-EM) to prefer self-edits that improve downstream performance after being applied via gradient updates.

papers.claim: ULOT predicts FUGW transport plans with competitive loss up to two orders of magnitude faster than classical solvers, and the predicted plan can be used as a warm start for classical solvers to accelerate their convergence.
papers.target: Prediction speedup (solver_time / ULOT_time) = 100x on SBM graph pairs, test set, direction
papers.gist: ULOT (Unsupervised Learning for Optimal Transport plan prediction between unbalanced graphs), NeurIPS 2025. A GNN is trained unsupervised to predict FUGW (Fused Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein) transport plans between graph pairs, giving near-solver loss at inference speed. Evaluated on simulated SBM graph pairs and on IBC fMRI surfaces; the headline is a competitive-loss / two-orders-of-magnitude-faster tradeoff vs classical BCD solvers.

papers.claim: CLAMP (Contrastive Learning As Manifold Packing) achieves competitive self-supervised learning performance by recasting representation learning as a neural manifold packing problem using a physics-inspired repulsive ellipsoid loss.
papers.target: Top-1 classification accuracy (%) = 90.21% on CIFAR-10 validation set, point estimate
papers.gist: CLAMP (Contrastive Learning As Manifold Packing) is a self-supervised representation-learning method that packs augmented views of each image onto per-image sub-manifolds via a repulsive-potential loss, evaluated by linear-probe classification accuracy on a frozen backbone.

papers.claim: The proposed geometric framework for momentum-based low-rank optimizers (DLRT-Adam and DLRT-HeavyBall) achieves convergence to low-rank optima with strong validation accuracy at high compression rates, outperforming naive application of momentum methods to low-rank parameterizations.
papers.target: Test accuracy = 79.01% on CIFAR-10 test set, point estimate
papers.gist: Presents DLRT-HeavyBall (Algorithm 1): a dynamical low-rank training method with heavy-ball momentum for compressing VGG16 during CIFAR-10 training, claiming compressed training matches full-rank HeavyBall accuracy at high compression.

papers.claim: 4D-LRM is the first large-scale 4D reconstruction model that takes input from unconstrained views and timestamps and renders arbitrary novel view-time combinations, enabling fast, high-quality 4D reconstruction from sparse inputs.
papers.target: PSNR (dB) = 27.443 on Consistent4D dataset (re-rendered), point estimate
papers.gist: 4D-LRM: a large-scale 4D reconstruction model that maps posed image sequences to per-pixel 4D Gaussians in a single feed-forward pass, trained on Objaverse4D object-level data and evaluated on the re-rendered Consistent4D benchmark under several camera setups (alternating canonical, fixed canonical, etc.) at 256 resolution.

papers.claim: ReasonFlux-PRM-7B selects higher quality trajectory-response data than existing PRMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B) and human-curated baselines, achieving 6.0% improvement on MATH500 and 6.1% on GPQA-Diamond in downstream SFT of smaller models.
papers.target: MATH500 accuracy = >80% (vs ~73% random-selection baseline; paper Table 84.8% for 7B-selected) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fine-tuned on ReasonFlux-PRM-selected data, threshold
papers.gist: ReasonFlux-PRM: a trajectory-aware process reward model. Headline offline-selection claim (Table SFT_results / existing_prm_dataselect_result): using ReasonFlux-PRM-7B to select the top-1K of 59K Gemini-distilled reasoning trajectories, then SFT-ing Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on that 1K for 5 epochs (lr=1e-5, wd=1e-4, max_seq_len=32768), reaches 84.8% MATH500 accuracy vs 78.8% for the human-curated s1k baseline and 68.4% for random selection.

papers.claim: Decomposable Flow Matching (DFM) improves visual generation quality over standard Flow Matching baselines through progressive multi-scale generation, achieving 35.2% FDD improvement on ImageNet-1K 512px under the same training compute.
papers.target: FID 10K = 29.56 on ImageNet-1K 512px, 10K samples, point estimate
papers.gist: Decomposable Flow Matching (DFM, NeurIPS 2025) decomposes image generation into a Laplacian-pyramid-like sequence of scales and trains flow matching independently at each scale, claiming faster convergence and better quality than standard single-scale flow matching (e.g. SiT).

papers.claim: ERDM outperforms EDM baselines for probabilistic forecasting, achieving approximately 50% better CRPS than EDM W=4 for long-range Navier-Stokes forecasts beyond timestep 15, with superior calibration.
papers.target: CRPS (mean across 64-timestep Navier-Stokes test rollout, 50-member ensemble) = 0.904×10^-2 (0.00904) on 5 Navier-Stokes test trajectories, 64 timesteps each, averaged over rollout, point estimate
papers.gist: Elucidated Rolling Diffusion Models (ERDM), a NeurIPS-2025 paper from UCSD and NVIDIA that ports the EDM recipe (noise schedule, preconditioning, loss weighting, Heun sampler) into a sliding-window rolling forecast setting. It claims ERDM beats conditional autoregressive EDM baselines on 2D Navier-Stokes and on ERA5 weather forecasting.

papers.claim: Extended Kalman Filter-based inference on differentiable Hodgkin-Huxley simulators can accurately recover membrane conductances and cell positions from extracellular voltage recordings alone.
papers.target: Recovery accuracy: estimated vs. true maximum conductances (bias and variance across 40 datasets) = negligible bias and variance, estimates closely matching ground truth across random seeds on 40 synthetic single-branch datasets, σ_obs=1µV, point estimate
papers.gist: Proposes using Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) based inference on differentiable Hodgkin-Huxley neuron simulators to recover biophysical membrane conductances (and cell geometry) directly from extracellular voltage recordings.

papers.claim: IPFormer achieves state-of-the-art vision-based 3D Panoptic Scene Completion on SemanticKITTI, surpassing all baselines in PQ-All (6.30) and PQ-dag (14.45) while reducing runtime to 0.33s (14x speedup vs 4.70s baselines).
papers.target: PQ-All (%) = 6.30 on SemanticKITTI validation set (sequence 11, 815 voxel grids), point estimate
papers.gist: IPFormer: vision-based 3D Panoptic Scene Completion on SemanticKITTI using context-adaptive instance proposals as transformer queries instead of a separate clustering stage. Headline table: PQ-All 6.30, PQ-dag 14.45, SQ-All 41.95, RQ-All 9.75, IoU 40.90, mIoU 15.33, with 0.33 s per frame runtime, a ~14x speedup over CGFormer+DBSCAN at 4.70 s.

papers.claim: SharpZO achieves up to 7% average gain over state-of-the-art forward-only methods for VLM prompt tuning using only forward passes (no backpropagation), with a two-stage optimization consisting of sharpness-aware CMA-ES warm-up followed by sparse ZO-SGD fine-tuning.
papers.target: test accuracy (%) = 79.42% on EuroSAT test set, point estimate
papers.gist: SharpZO: forward-only (gradient-free) prompt tuning for CLIP. Stage 1 is a sharpness-aware CMA-ES warm-up over a 512-dim intrinsic prompt space (population 40, sigma 0.4, rho 0.1, CGE-estimated smoothness); at a change point the population is merged into a single vector and stage 2 runs sparse zeroth-order SGD with Z-score-based pruning. Evaluated across CLIP classification benchmarks with a frozen ViT-B/16 backbone.

papers.claim: AsymDSD achieves state-of-the-art 3D object recognition by combining masked point modeling with invariance learning through asymmetric dual self-distillation, reaching 90.53% accuracy on the hardest ScanObjectNN split (PB_T50_RS), a 5.35% improvement over the Point-MAE baseline.
papers.target: Overall accuracy (%) on ScanObjectNN PB_T50_RS test split = 90.53% on ScanObjectNN PB_T50_RS test split, point estimate
papers.gist: AsymDSD: asymmetric self-distillation with masked modeling for point-cloud self-supervised learning. A teacher/student ViT encoder pair is pretrained on ShapeNet with a joint latent self-distillation plus masked-modeling objective, then the teacher encoder is transferred to downstream shape classification. The headline transfer result is full fine-tuning on ScanObjectNN's hardest split.

papers.claim: Hippocampal place cells auto-associate sensory inputs with grid cell patterns, enabling cue-triggered goal retrieval, grid-based path planning that generalizes to novel routes, and reconstruction of sensory experiences along planned trajectories.
papers.target: L2 distance from decoded position to target position (cm) = ~0 cm after convergence (trajectories converge to goal representation) on 100x100cm simulated arena, nearest neighbor decoding on aggregated ratemaps, point estimate
papers.gist: REMI: a recurrent 'HC-MEC' RNN model (1120 units: 288 grid cells + 32 speed cells + 32 direction cells + 256 spatially-modulated sensory cells (SMC) + 512 unsupervised hippocampal-place-cell (HPC) units) that auto-associates sensory observations with grid-cell patterns, enabling cue-triggered recall of a goal location.

papers.claim: Adversarial attacks on verbal confidence (both perturbation-based VCA-TF, VCA-TB and jailbreak-based ConfidenceTriggers) can significantly reduce LLM confidence scores and cause high rates of answer changes.
papers.target: % affected samples with confidence reduction = 7.0% on TruthfulQA/Llama-3-8B/Base, threshold
papers.gist: 'On the Robustness of Verbal Confidence of LLMs in Adversarial Attacks' (NeurIPS 2025): proposes Verbal Confidence Attacks (VCA), including a perturbation-based variant VCA-TF (a TextFooler-style importance-scored synonym-substitution attack, semantically gated by Universal Sentence Encoder cosine similarity) that degrades an LLM's self-reported verbal confidence.

papers.claim: CogVLA achieves state-of-the-art performance with 97.4% success rate on LIBERO benchmark and 70.0% on real-world tasks, while reducing training costs by 2.5x and inference latency by 2.8x compared to OpenVLA through instruction-driven routing and sparsification.
papers.target: Task success rate = 98.6% on LIBERO-Spatial benchmark (10 tasks, 50 demonstrations each), point estimate
papers.gist: Proposes CogVLA, a vision-language-action model that prunes roughly half of the visual tokens per layer via an instruction-conditioned Learned-Foveal-Pruning (LFP) router plus a FiLM-conditioned vision backbone and aggregator, fine-tuned from OpenVLA-7B with LoRA, aiming for lower training cost with LIBERO manipulation performance competitive with or above OpenVLA.

papers.claim: CoUn achieves better machine unlearning effectiveness than state-of-the-art baselines, with an average gap of 0.25 compared to the Retrain model on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 under 10% random forget ratio.
papers.target: Average Gap (lower is better) = 0.25 on CIFAR-10 test set, 10% random forget data, 10 trials averaged, direction
papers.gist: CoUn is a machine-unlearning method that fine-tunes a trained classifier with a supervised loss plus a contrastive-learning regularizer to erase a designated forget-set from a ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 model while keeping retain and test accuracy close to a gold-standard retrained-from-scratch model.

papers.claim: The paper introduces a trajectory-based backdoor attack against end-to-end autonomous driving systems using temporal logic specifications, demonstrating that offline RL agents are vulnerable to such attacks with significant drops in reward and high mission violation rates when triggers are present.
papers.target: Poisoned MVR (mission violation rate) = 1.00 on MetaDrive Easy task, 100 trajectories, point estimate
papers.gist: A temporal-logic-verified, multi-vehicle trajectory backdoor attack against offline-RL end-to-end autonomous driving agents: a sync-bypass trigger (two attacker vehicles bypass the ego) causes a poisoned Coptidice agent to execute a dangerous sudden left turn.

papers.claim: Fine-tuned 7B parameter LLaMA model with LoRA on AVHuBERT-extracted visual features achieves state-of-the-art lip reading performance on LRS3-Data, LRS2-Train, and VoxCeleb2 datasets withWERs of 3.0%, 4.3%, and 9.1% respectively.
papers.target: exact = exact on full, direction
papers.gist: MoME (Mixture of Matryoshka Experts) for Audio-Visual Speech Recognition, NeurIPS 2025: a sparse-MoE LoRA architecture on Llama 3.2-1B/3B/3.1-8B fusing AVHuBERT audio-visual features, evaluated on LRS2 and LRS3 ASR/AVSR/VSR tables. No VoxCeleb2 evaluation and no 7B+LoRA (non-MoE) configuration appears anywhere in the paper.

papers.claim: Spectral batch selection using effective rank R_eff as an anisotropy proxy (Greedy-64 sampler) improves contrastive learning convergence speed by ~15% in wall-clock time vs. random sampling on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100, with no loss in final top-1 accuracy.
papers.target: convergence speed = wall-clock time to reach 90% of Pool-P3 final top-1 accuracy = Greedy-64 converges faster than random sampling (direction); paper reports ~15% time-to-target reduction on ImageNet-100, 'similar gains' on CIFAR-10 on CIFAR-10 (SimCLR); provisional — CIFAR-10 anchor is direction-only, the numeric 15% is ImageNet-100, direction
papers.gist: A spectral batch-selection method for contrastive learning: batches are chosen to control the effective rank (R_eff, an anisotropy proxy of the embedding Gram matrix) of each SimCLR batch, either via a balanced sampling pool (Pool-P3, targeting an R_eff window) or an exact greedy diversity maximizer (Greedy-64), instead of uniform random sampling.

papers.claim: MaNGO (Meta Neural Graph Operator) uses meta-learning with Conditional Neural Processes to enable Graph Network Simulators to adapt to unseen physical parameters using only a few context examples, achieving Full Rollout MSE close to an oracle model that has access to ground-truth simulation parameters.
papers.target: Full Rollout MSE = 1.259e-6 on Deformable Plate Easy test split (100 trajectories), point estimate
papers.gist: MaNGO is a meta-learning graph network simulator (Conditional Neural Process plus GNN decoder) that adapts to unseen material/physical parameters from a few context trajectories, evaluated on physical-simulation benchmarks including a deformable-plate manipulation task.

papers.claim: The multiply robust (MR) estimator for the always-survivor value function is consistent under any one of five different nuisance model specification scenarios, providing robustness to partial misspecification that standard approaches (outcome regression, IPW, AIPW) lack.
papers.target: Bias of MR estimator value estimate for always-survivor value function = -0.20 on Simulation study, Scenario M1, Table 1, point estimate
papers.gist: Proposes a multiply robust (MR) estimator for off-policy value functions with censoring and truncation-by-death, and demonstrates its consistency under partial nuisance-model misspecification via a Monte Carlo simulation study (Simulation 1).

papers.claim: MORE (MOdel REbalancing) significantly improves generalization for tail classes in long-tailed recognition by rebalancing model parameter space through low-rank decomposition, without increasing inference costs.
papers.target: Top-1 accuracy (%) = 65.9% on CIFAR-100-LT (All classes), point estimate
papers.gist: MORE (MOdel REbalancing): improves tail-class generalization in long-tailed recognition by adding a low-rank tail-parameter delta (B^t A^t) to a base model's convolutions, trained against a discrepancy loss with a sinusoidal amplitude schedule, then merging the tail delta into the base weights at inference. Evaluated as ProCo+MORE on CIFAR-100-LT IF=10.

papers.claim: Locally minimax-optimal private samplers consistently outperform global minimax samplers under both pure LDP and ν-GLDP settings across all privacy regimes.
papers.target: Worst-case total variation distance = Local sampler TV < Global sampler TV (local ~0.123 < global ~0.123? code must verify) on Finite space X=[k] with uniform reference μ_k, worst-case over local neighborhood N_γ(μ_k), direction
papers.gist: Studies locally minimax-optimal private samplers under local differential privacy (LDP and nu-GLDP), showing they consistently achieve lower worst-case f-divergence than global minimax samplers.

papers.claim: RADiAnce significantly outperforms baseline models on protein binder design tasks, achieving higher amino acid recovery (AAR), lower RMSD, better binding affinity (ΔΔG), and improved interaction pattern recovery (ISM) for both antibody CDR and peptide sequence-structure co-design.
papers.target: ISM (Interaction Site Match, %) = 52.15% on LNR test benchmark (93 peptide-protein complexes), point estimate
papers.gist: RADiAnce is a RAG-augmented latent diffusion model for peptide/antibody/protein-fragment binder design, conditioned on retrieved interface features.

papers.claim: Salient concept-aware (SCA) embedding model trained with angular margin loss enables personalized image generation for data augmentation that better preserves class-discriminative features while aligning with text prompts, yielding improved downstream classification accuracy across fine-grained vision datasets.
papers.target: Downstream classification Top-1 accuracy (%) = 89.68 on CUB200-2011 test set, direction
papers.gist: SCA-GDA: train a salient concept-aware (SCA) embedding model with angular-margin loss, use it to condition SDXL fine-tuning for personalized synthetic-image generation, and augment classifier training data with the synthetic images to improve fine-grained visual classification (CUB200-2011 RN50: 89.68% vs 86.62% vanilla baseline).

papers.claim: CKA-RL outperforms state-of-the-art continual reinforcement learning methods by achieving 4.20% improvement in overall performance and 8.02% improvement in forward transfer, by maintaining a task-specific knowledge vector pool and dynamically reusing historical knowledge to adapt to new tasks.
papers.target: Average performance (PERF.) = 0.7923 on Freeway task sequence (8 modes), point estimate
papers.gist: CKA-RL is a continual reinforcement learning method that maintains a pool of reusable network modules, selected by centered kernel alignment (CKA) similarity, to mitigate catastrophic forgetting across a sequence of RL tasks.

papers.claim: DynaInfer infers environment specifications from prediction errors of fixed neural networks, enabling environment assignments directly from data without manual labels, outperforming existing environment assignment techniques and converging rapidly to true labels.
papers.target: test MSE on LV trajectory forecasting with inferred environment assignments = paper reports 7.93e-5; bar = test MSE < 1e-3 (within one order of magnitude) AND environment assignments converge to the true 9-environment labels on LV 9-environment experiment, label-free environment inference, threshold
papers.gist: DynaInfer: a method that infers latent environment labels for multi-environment dynamical-systems forecasting (Lotka-Volterra, Gray-Scott, Navier-Stokes, Robot Motion) from the prediction errors of per-environment neural nets, then plugs those inferred labels into either a LEADS or CoDA backbone. Code released at github.com/shixuanliu-andy/DynaInfer.

papers.claim: Thompson Sampling with multi-output GP models for reinforcement learning in finite-horizon MDPs achieves sublinear cumulative regret, confirming the theoretical O(sqrt(KH*Gamma(KH))) bound.
papers.target: cumulative regret growth pattern = sublinear (grows slower than linear O(T), flattens/curves downward over episodes) on synthetic navigation MDP environment, direction

papers.claim: FineRS achieves state-of-the-art performance on instruction-guided reasoning and segmentation of small objects in high-resolution images through a two-stage MLLM-based reinforcement learning framework.
papers.target: gIoU (generic Intersection over Union) = 55.1 on FineRS-4k test set (2,427 samples, all object sizes), point estimate
papers.gist: FineRS: a two-stage MLLM reinforcement-learning framework for instruction-guided reasoning and segmentation of small objects in high-resolution images. A global search/exploration stage (GSE, Qwen2.5-VL-7B at 1920x1080) proposes a coarse box plus an answer, a local patch refinement stage (LPR, 512x512 crop) emits a refined box plus points as JSON, and SAM2 turns that into a mask. Table 1 on the authors' own FineRS-4k benchmark (2427 test samples) reports gIoU 55.1 / cIoU 46.5 all-sizes and MVQA 83.3 / OVQA 56.7.

papers.claim: FairImagen, a post-hoc FairPCA-based debiasing framework applied to CLIP prompt embeddings, significantly improves gender fairness in text-to-image generation while preserving acceptable image quality and prompt fidelity compared to baseline Stable Diffusion and other post-hoc debiasing methods.
papers.target: gender fairness score (0-1, higher = more balanced gender distribution) = 0.560 on 100-prompt test set / 30-prompt dev set, gender debiasing, point estimate
papers.gist: FairImagen post-hoc debiases CLIP prompt embeddings via FairPCA to reduce gender bias in text-to-image generation (Stable Diffusion 3), trading a small amount of image-text alignment for fairness gains.

papers.claim: AniDS (Anisotropic Variational Autoencoder for 3D Molecular Denoising) generates structure-aware anisotropic noise distributions that improve molecular force field learning, achieving 8.9% average improvement on MD17 and 6.2% on OC22 for force prediction compared to isotropic/homoscedastic denoising baselines.
papers.target: Force MAE (kcal/mol/Å) = 0.102 on MD17 Aspirin test set, point estimate
papers.gist: AniDS pretrains an anisotropic VAE denoiser on PCQM4Mv2 3D molecular conformers, then finetunes an EquiformerV2 force-field model on MD17 per-molecule trajectories; the paper claims the PCQM4Mv2 pretraining improves downstream force-prediction accuracy.

papers.claim: MiCADangelo reconstructs fully parametric CAD models from 3D scans using 2D cross-sections and predicts sketch constraints, achieving state-of-the-art performance on DeepCAD and Fusion360 benchmarks (Med. CD 0.20, IoU 80.6 on DeepCAD test set).
papers.target: Median Chamfer Distance (x10^3) = 0.20 on DeepCAD test set, point estimate
papers.gist: MiCADangelo reconstructs fully parametric, constrained CAD models from 3D scans via 2D cross-section slicing, plane detection, and sketch-constraint prediction (built on a 'Davinci' sketch-parameterization backbone), evaluated on the DeepCAD test set.

papers.claim: MERGE unifies image generation and depth estimation by adding pluggable converters to a fixed pre-trained T2I diffusion model, preserving generation ability while enabling zero-shot depth estimation with only ~12% additional trainable parameters.
papers.target: absolute relative error (A.Rel) = 7.5 on NYUv2 test set (zero-shot depth estimation), threshold
papers.gist: MERGE: parameter-efficient conversion of a frozen text-to-image diffusion transformer (PixArt-XL-2-512x512) into a dense-prediction model via ~110M learnable converter modules, trained on 74K Hypersim+VKITTI samples and evaluated zero-shot. Table 1 row 'ours-B' reports NYUv2 depth A.Rel 7.5 and delta1 94.2 with 110M (18%) learnable parameters, following Marigold's preprocessing and least-squares alignment conventions.

papers.claim: TAMI framework (with LTE log time encoding and TRC link history aggregation modules) consistently improves temporal link prediction AP of state-of-the-art TGNNs across 13 datasets in both transductive and inductive settings.
papers.target: Average Precision (AP) in percent = 98.89 on Wikipedia test set, 5 runs, random negative sampling, point estimate
papers.gist: TAMI augments temporal graph link-prediction backbones (e.g. GraphMixer) with an LTE time encoding and a TRC memory module to improve temporal link prediction accuracy.

papers.claim: SemCoT achieves state-of-the-art performance in both efficiency and effectiveness compared to existing implicit CoT methods on reasoning tasks, by jointly optimizing token-level generation speed and preserving semantic alignment with ground-truth reasoning.
papers.target: answer accuracy on SVAMP test set = ~46% (paper Table 1, Llama/Sheared-LLaMA small-config row) on SVAMP 300-example test set, 1 implicit token, point estimate
papers.gist: SemCoT trains a lightweight generator to produce compressed, implicit chain-of-thought tokens that approximate full chain-of-thought reasoning at much lower inference cost.

papers.claim: EA3D enables online open-world 3D object extraction from streaming videos without geometric priors or pose input, achieving high-quality reconstruction (PSNR 25.8) and scene understanding (mIoU 46.3) on ScanNet.
papers.target: PSNR (peak signal-to-noise ratio, dB) = 25.8 on ScanNet dataset (10 indoor RGB sequences), point estimate
papers.gist: EA3D: Online Open-World 3D Object Extraction from Streaming Videos (VDIGPKU; accepted NeurIPS 2025) proposes an online, pose-free pipeline for open-world 3D object extraction from RGB video, combining an online feature-Gaussian-splatting backbone (HiCoM-based) with vision-foundation-model guidance (Grounded-SAM/CLIP) and online odometry (Cut3R/DPVO), evaluated on ScanNet across reconstruction, segmentation, 3D bounding box, and semantic occupancy tasks.

papers.claim: MoGE (Modelic Generative Exploration) effectively bridges exploration and policy learning in off-policy RL through diffusion-based critical state generation and a one-step imagination world model, leading to remarkable gains in both sample efficiency and performance across complex control tasks.
papers.target: Total Average Return (TAR) = 891.7 ± 19.1 on DeepMind Control Suite Humanoid-walk task, averaged over 3 seeds, point estimate
papers.gist: Proposes MoGE (Modelic Generative Exploration): a classifier-guided diffusion model that generates 'critical-state' transitions, mixed into DSAC (Distributional Soft Actor-Critic) updates to improve exploration, tested on DeepMind Control Suite Humanoid-walk.

papers.claim: LeMiCa achieves efficient acceleration of diffusion-based video generation through lexicographic minimax path caching, delivering 2.9x speedup on Latte while maintaining visual quality with LPIPS of 0.05 on Open-Sora.
papers.target: Latency speedup ratio = 2.59x on Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B 480p single-video generation, point estimate
papers.gist: LeMiCa: Lexicographic Minimax Path Caching for training-free acceleration of diffusion video generation. It formulates denoising-step caching as a shortest-path problem over the step graph and picks a budget-B subset of steps to fully compute, replaying cached residuals for the rest, minimising worst-case error rather than average error. Paper headline results are on Latte, Open-Sora 1.2 and CogVideoX (2.9x on Latte, LPIPS 0.05 on Open-Sora); the Wan2.1 numbers exist only in the released repo.

papers.claim: GeneFlow's rectified flow-based approach outperforms diffusion-based baseline method in generating histopathological images from single-cell gene expression, achieving FID scores 3-6x lower.
papers.target: FID of generated histopathology images vs. real (lower is better) = Rectified Flow FID clearly below the diffusion baseline (paper Table 1: RF 20.73 +/- 8.45 vs Diffusion 171.06 +/- 81.98 on Xenium_C1); anchor = RF FID far under diffusion FID on the same sample on Xenium_C1 single-cell model, FID over the held-out cells, direction
papers.gist: GeneFlow generates histopathology images from single-cell gene-expression profiles via a rectified-flow model, claimed to strongly outperform a diffusion baseline on image fidelity.

papers.claim: HMVLM with MoE LoRA and zero expert preserves foundation model knowledge while achieving strong text-to-motion performance on HumanML3D (R-precision Top-3 of 0.785).
papers.target: R precision Top-3 = 0.785 on HumanML3D test set, point estimate
papers.gist: HMVLM: Human Motion-Vision-Language Model via MoE LoRA -- a text-to-motion generation model using a body-part motion tokenizer (5 body-part VQ codebooks) plus a Vicuna-7B-v1.5 backbone wrapped with MoE-LoRA (4 trainable LoRA experts plus a frozen zero expert, CLIP-gated), evaluated on HumanML3D.

papers.claim: FIOC-WM learns a two-level factorization (object-level with explicit interactions + attribute-level static/dynamic) that improves policy-learning sample efficiency and generalization over world-model baselines in object-centric reinforcement learning.
papers.target: policy learning success rate = 0.95 ± 0.03 on OpenAI Gym Fetch Task 1 (2-push), evaluated over 5-10 random seeds, point estimate
papers.gist: FIOC-WM: a factored interactive object-centric world model for object-centric reinforcement learning, learning DINO-v2-based object-centric latents with an ACD-style variational interaction mask and hierarchical (high-level interaction selection + low-level MPC/PPO) policy learning.

papers.claim: Differentiable Hierarchical Tokenization (dHT) is an end-to-end differentiable tokenizer that adapts to image content with pixel-level granularity and is backward-compatible with existing ViT architectures for retrofitting pretrained models, achieving competitive ImageNet classification and out-of-the-box raster-to-vector conversion.
papers.target: SSIM reconstruction quality = 0.8541 on DiffVG-5 benchmark (5 COCO test images), point estimate
papers.gist: dHT is a tokenizer/model that segments images into superpixel-like regions and vectorizes them into SVGs (Bezier paths per region), aiming to reproduce raster images as compact vector graphics comparable to classical vectorization baselines like DiffVG.

papers.claim: SceneDesigner achieves multi-object 9-DoF pose control (location, size, orientation) in image generation with significantly improved controllability and quality over existing methods like LOOSECONTROL and Continuous 3D Words.
papers.target: Orientation accuracy at 22.5° tolerance (Acc@22.5°) = 89.47% on ObjectPose-Single-Front benchmark (247 validation samples from COCO with 9D pose annotations), point estimate
papers.gist: SceneDesigner: controllable multi-object image generation with 9-DoF pose manipulation. An SD3.5-medium ControlNet is conditioned on a CNOCS map (per-pixel normalized cuboid-surface coordinates encoding each object's 9D pose), trained in two stages: 45K iterations of supervised ControlNet training, then a 5K-iteration RL finetune whose reward is an Orient-Anything orientation score. Evaluated on a self-built ObjectPose benchmark carved from COCO validation.

papers.claim: RLNLC formulates noisy label correction as a reinforcement learning problem and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks by learning a policy network via actor-critic methods to iteratively correct noisy training labels.
papers.target: Test accuracy (%) = 97.3 on CIFAR10-IDN test set, point estimate
papers.gist: RLNLC (Reinforcement Learning for Noisy Label Correction): an actor-critic RL policy observes each training instance's kNN neighborhood in embedding space and learns to decide, per-instance, whether to relabel it to the majority-neighbor label, iteratively cleaning a noisy training set before a final classifier is fit on the cleaned labels.

papers.claim: DA-SIP achieves 2.6-4.4x reduction in total computation time while maintaining task success rates comparable to fixed maximum-computation baselines for robot manipulation tasks.
papers.target: task success rate = 100% on RoboMimic Lift task, threshold
papers.gist: DA-SIP (Difficulty-Aware Stochastic Interpolant Policy): a flow/stochastic-interpolant imitation-learning robot policy claiming strong manipulation performance with very few (down to 1) inference/denoising steps, evaluated on RoboMimic benchmark tasks including Lift.

papers.claim: Pre-trained video diffusion models inherently learn motion representations suitable for tracking similar-looking objects without task-specific training, achieving up to 6-point improvement over recent self-supervised approaches on established benchmarks.
papers.target: J&F mean (Jaccard + F-measure average, %) = 77.6% on DAVIS-2017 validation set (30 videos, 2023 frames), point estimate
papers.gist: TED: pre-trained video diffusion models (I2VGen-XL) inherently learn motion representations suitable for tracking similar-looking objects, without task-specific training. The method fuses an appearance branch (ADM diffusion features, following DIFT's protocol) with a motion branch (I2VGen-XL 3D-UNet decoder features) via label propagation for semi-supervised video object segmentation.

papers.claim: Shortcut features correspond to eigenfunctions of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) with larger eigenvalues; features with larger eigenvalues are learned faster due to spectral bias and have a larger influence on the neural network output even after training convergence.
papers.target: NTK availability A(K,g) = g^T K g / (||g||^2 ||K||_F) for shortcut (color) vs ground-truth label vectors = availability(shortcut) > availability(ground-truth) at step 1000; the qualitative ordering is the falsifiable core of the eigenvalue/spectral-bias claim on Colored-MNIST shortcut-learning experiment, empirical finite-width NTK, direction
papers.gist: A theory/empirical paper introducing an 'availability' metric A(K,g) = g^T K g / (||g||^2 ||K||_F) built from the empirical finite-width NTK, used to show that shortcut labels are more 'available' to gradient descent than ground-truth labels early in training -- validated empirically on a Colored-MNIST shortcut-learning setup.
