audit.rationale: This is a fully executed, honestly reported reproduction attempt for a paper with no released code, checkpoints, or scoring scripts for the specific target algorithm (Algorithm 1, DLRT-HeavyBall). The agent reconstructed the algorithm faithfully from the paper's LaTeX description, validated its port with a chain-rule numerical identity and cross-checks against the authors' available reference repositories, and executed the exact target protocol (VGG16-BN, CIFAR-10, tau=0.1, initial rank 150, 20 epochs, lr=1e-3, gamma=0.9) plus an extensive hyperparameter batch and mechanistic root-cause diagnosis, all backed by real GPU training logs with plausible runtimes and realistic, fluctuating training curves; the reproducible AdamW (89.6% vs. paper's 89.82%) and HeavyBall (78.43% vs. paper's 78.98%, at a tuned lr) baselines corroborate that the overall protocol (data, architecture, initialization) was implemented correctly. The measured DLRT-HeavyBall result (10.0-10.24%, chance level) is nowhere near the 79.01% target under any tested configuration, and the agent's own 'not_reproduced' verdict matches this cited evidence exactly with no hardcoding, self-scoring, retrieved-answer, or stale-artifact flags found. This matches the grading protocol's score-5 anchor for a code-blocked paper where the agent reconstructed the protocol in good faith, ran full coverage, and honestly disclosed a divergent result. The one open question — whether the extreme, total failure reflects a genuine algorithmic property or a subtle bug in this from-scratch reimplementation (since the authors' own reference DLRT lineage differs structurally from Algorithm 1 as specified) — is disclosed by the agent itself.

runs.claim: The proposed geometric framework for momentum-based low-rank optimizers (DLRT-Adam and DLRT-HeavyBall) achieves convergence to low-rank optima with strong validation accuracy at high compression rates, outperforming naive application of momentum methods to low-rank parameterizations.
runs.target: Test accuracy = 79.01% on CIFAR-10 test set, point estimate

flags.evidence: The pinned the match target supplied was 'threshold', but reference/latex/neurips_2025.tex Table 1 (lines 664 and 771) reports 7.0% strictly as a single measured table cell with no threshold/floor language anywhere in the paper's text near this table; the pinned configuration text also frames this as 'measuring % affected samples... on TruthfulQA', i.e. a point estimate to match, not a floor to clear. Grading this cell as a '>=7.0%' threshold would let any large overshoot trivially pass, contradicting both the paper's framing and the agent's own honest 'not_reproduced' conclusion, so the match target was corrected to point_estimate with the standard ±5% relative default per rubric the match criterion and the correction is recorded here for human review.

However, because no official code or artifacts were ever released for this paper, several protocol elements (Base CEM prompt text, USE similarity gate, exact checkpoint) had to be reconstructed rather than reused, and the measured attack effect (35.5-45.0% affected) is roughly 5-6x the paper's specific Table-1 cell (7.0%) under both candidate-generation variants tried, a large and honestly disclosed divergence rather than a near-miss. flags.evidence: MORE's official code repo (IMLSH/MORE) contains only a README stating 'The code is coming soon' (workspace/repo_more/README.md, verified via live git clone in commands.log line 10 and re-checked at line 175). The agent reconstructed MOREConv2d, the discrepancy loss, and the sinusoidal schedule purely from the paper's equations with no reference implementation to validate normalization/init choices, as it explicitly discloses in REPORT.md section 6 ('the precise 65.9 could not be reproduced from first principles with certainty').

The paper states the amplitude ablation is optimal at A'=A/C≈2.0, i.e. A=200 for C=100 classes (reference/latex/Tex/Experiments.tex line 203). At that faithful setting the agent's MORE port produced 64.64% (run_more_kaiming.log:839), statistically indistinguishable from the 64.67% baseline. Only by sweeping to a much smaller, non-canonical amplitude (A=25) did the agent obtain 65.13% (run_more_a25.log:839), which it then reports as the headline 'best' MORE result. This is transparently disclosed in REPORT.md's full results table (not concealed), but it means the number nominally clearing the tolerance band was obtained by deviating from the paper's own prescribed operating point, while the faithful configuration directly fails to show the claimed effect.

audit.rationale: This is a genuine, fully-executed, honestly-disclosed reproduction attempt on the correct benchmark (CIFAR-100-LT IF=10, ResNet32, ProCo baseline, rank r=0.1), with real 200-epoch training runs traceable end-to-end through commands.log timestamps/durations, per-epoch training logs, and architecture-consistent checkpoints — no hardcoding, no self-scoring, no wrong split or dataset. However, the paper's official MORE code was never released (independently verified via a live clone showing only a 'coming soon' README), forcing the agent to reimplement the novel low-rank rebalancing mechanism from equations alone with no ground truth to validate against. Critically, when the agent ran MORE at the paper's own specified 'optimal' hyperparameter (A=200, derived directly from the paper's stated A'≈2.0), it measured essentially no improvement over baseline (64.64% vs 64.67%) — directly failing to reproduce the causal claim at the correct operating point. Only a disclosed batch to a smaller, non-canonical amplitude (A=25) produced a partial improvement (65.13%, roughly half the paper's claimed +0.9pp gain) that happens to fall inside an overly loose default ±5% tolerance band — a band so loose that even the flat, unmodified baseline clears it, making the mechanical 'pass' non-diagnostic of the actual claim. The agent's own honest conclusion ('not_reproduced') matches this deeper reading. This profile — a real code-blocked situation, good-faith full-coverage reconstruction across multiple configurations, and transparent disclosure of a diverging/uncertain result — matches the grading protocol's a score of 5. Two med-severity provenance flags (unvalidated reimplementation of the paper's central mechanism; best-of-N hyperparameter reporting that contradicts the faithful-config result) further support keeping this below the 'reproduced' or 'near-reproduction' bands. No high-severity flags were found, so the run is not disqualified, and the self-report does not overstate its own evidence.

The trajectory/agent.full.log (lines ~479-505) shows the agent only read the README's setup instructions but the commands.log contains no invocation of the 'mixinputs setup'/'mixinputs enable' CLI. The patch module logs 'Patching the installed vllm to enable Mixture of Inputs' at INFO level when triggered (agent set MIXINPUTS_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO) - this string and any mention of 'mixinputs'/'patching' returns 0 matches across evidence/moi_eval_full.log, moi_eval_run.log, moi_eval_4gpu.log, moi_eval_output.log, and standard_eval_full.log. Therefore vllm_patch.py's monkey-patch of vllm.v1.worker.gpu_model_runner.GPUModelRunner was never applied in either run; both 'MoI' and 'Standard' arms used stock unpatched vLLM sampling differing only by top_p (0.4 vs 1.0). However, the claim's actual experiment (Fuse-and-Refine on GS-LRM, or even a correctly-weighted DepthSplat sibling) was never demonstrably underway: the final measurement comes from a hand-rolled architecture with zero checkpoint weights loaded, evaluated on only 2 scenes, and is explicitly disclosed as unrelated to the target quantity. No HIGH-severity the provenance check flags apply — no hardcoding, no self-scoring against a fabricated key, no echoed prose number, no stale artifact passed off as fresh, no benchmark answer-key retrieval — so the run is not disqualified to 0, but the outcome is a genuine execution failure honestly reported, landing at score 2.

Per rubric, sanctioned sibling-checkpoint substitution requires 'the nearest released checkpoint of the same method'; substituting a rival baseline method is a materially different experiment, not a sanctioned substitution.

Even for the substituted baseline, the pipeline's own measured number (24.59% gIoU) misses the paper's reported figure for that exact checkpoint (58.3% gIoU) by 33.7 points; the agent used ignore_mismatched_sizes=True due to visual-config mismatches, a self-probed prompt format, and JSON-bbox-to-rectangle parsing instead of the model's native polygon output — an unvalidated, ad hoc reimplementation. This is disclosed honestly in REPORT.md §5-6 rather than concealed, keeping severity low, but it further shows the eval pipeline used cannot be trusted as a stand-in signal for the claim.

audit.rationale: The run performed genuine, verifiable execution (a full 779-sample inference pass over ReasonSeg-test with saved per-sample outputs and matching log traces), so this is not a non-attempt, and no fabricated or self-scored number was placed in the target slot — the agent correctly reports the SAM-R1 target as unmeasured, ruling out score 0 and score 1. That substitute evaluation additionally badly underperforms its own paper-reported reference (24.59% vs 58.3% gIoU), so it offers no useful proxy signal either. flags.evidence: The paper's exact checkpoint (tabdpt1_1.safetensors, 16 layers/768 dim, matching the paper's stated 78M model) was released on HuggingFace and successfully downloaded by the agent (agent.full.log ~line 706, ~798-799); the compatible v1.1 codebase (TabDPT-inference-v1_1, tag v1.1.0) was also cloned. The claimed 'incompatibility' (gpu_step_0007.log 'Missing key enc_cell_dim') only shows loading v1_1 weights with the WRONG v1.2 codebase, which trivially fails by construction. When the agent later attempted to load the converted v1_1 checkpoint via the correct v1.1 codebase (agent.full.log lines ~8237-8262), the load crashed on an unrelated OS error ('libgomp: Thread creation failed: Resource temporarily unavailable') -- not an architecture/config error -- and was never retried despite ~31.7 of 32 allotted H100-hours remaining. The agent's own report states 'our v1.2 result already clears the bar, so we do not switch' (evidence/REPORT.md §5), confirming the model swap was made for convenience after a single aborted attempt, not because the exact checkpoint was proven unusable. tabdpt1_2 ('TabDPT-Turbo') is additionally documented by the authors as covered by a separate paper ('our TabDPT-Turbo paper', https://openreview.net/forum?id=Y00pwFyrHR, quoted agent.full.log line 470) with a structurally different architecture (32 layers/512 dim + regression-bin head + column-attention + thinking-rows + LAWA averaging) and different training recipe. This is not a sanctioned sibling-checkpoint substitution under the rubric, which requires the exact checkpoint to be genuinely unretrievable and explicitly forbids substitutions that change model size/method or swap away from a checkpoint that was retrievable -- both conditions are violated here.

audit.rationale: Although the numerical pipeline in this run is legitimately executed and its aggregation independently reproducible (real per-dataset GPU inference logs, matching CSV row counts, and a bootstrap-CI recomputation from raw outputs that exactly matches the reported summary.json), the graded value was produced by evaluating a materially different model -- TabDPT-Turbo (v1.2), documented by the authors as the subject of a separate paper with a different architecture and training recipe -- rather than the exact 78M/16-layer TabDPT checkpoint that is the actual subject of the central claim in 2410.18164's Table 1. That correct checkpoint was released on HuggingFace and was in fact downloaded by the agent, and a compatible older codebase (v1.1) was also cloned; the agent's single attempt to load and evaluate the correct checkpoint crashed for an unrelated OS resource reason (thread-creation limit) and was never retried, with the agent's own report candidly stating it did not switch back because the substitute model 'already clears the bar.' This is precisely the scenario the rubric singles out as disqualifying rather than sanctioned (checkpoint was retrievable; model size/architecture changed), constituting a 'materially different experiment than the claim' -- a HIGH-severity the provenance check flag that caps the score at 0 regardless of how faithfully the substitute model's own numbers were computed.
